# Coupled Control-Loop Tuning and Diagnosis (Provisional)

## Scope and Model Boundary

F04 (#11788) tunes gain and task-weight parameters of the F02 distributed
controller over multiple forward-dynamics trials. The current implementation
is a bounded **synthetic** method demonstration. It calls the actual F02
controller at every integration boundary in a two-coordinate mass-coupled
plant, but does not yet fit a measured swing or qualify a native engine. The
nominal feedforward, reference trajectory, state estimator, actuator map,
contact policy, model parameters, phase boundaries, and observation protocol
must be frozen before tuning. The controller's information pattern in this
fixture is exact simulated state, not delayed or noisy measured motion.

For phase $p$, group $g$, trial $r$, and gain/weight vector $x$, the evaluator
returns a nonnegative squared tracking loss $L_{rpg}(x)$, applied-input effort
$E_r(x)$, robustness penalty $R_r(x)$, constraint violation $C_r(x)$ and
saturation fraction $S_r(x)$. The training objective is

$$
J(x)=\sum_g\operatorname{mean}_{r,p}L_{rpg}(x)
 + w_E\operatorname{mean}_r E_r(x)
 + w_R\operatorname{mean}_r R_r(x)
 + w_0\left\|D^{-1}(x-x_0)\right\|_2^2,
$$

where $D$ contains declared positive parameter scales. Each parameter has a
finite lower/upper bound. The evaluator is responsible for integrating the
same coupled plant, applying the post-limit actuator commands and measuring
the declared contact, tracking and disturbance outputs. In particular, a
contact reaction is a plant output unless a run is explicitly externally
forced; it is never silently added as an independently controlled input.

## Bounded Optimization and Acceptance

The algorithm takes bounded L-BFGS-B steps group by group as an initialization,
then performs one bounded joint refinement. Every stage has a finite function
evaluation budget and a scaled trust region. A checkpoint records its solver
status, attempted parameters, objective, per-group loss, constraint violation,
saturation fraction, evaluations and accept/reject reason. Nonconvergence,
constraint violation, cross-group regression and lack of objective improvement
prevent promotion. Returned numerical evidence arrays are detached read-only
snapshots so later caller edits cannot change a reported outcome. Joint
refinement is needed because block independence is a
hypothesis; a group can improve alone while degrading the coupled plant.

Training and holdout trials are declared separately. The holdout report
contains the full coupled controller and each declared reduced grouping,
including tracking RMSE, effort, robustness, constraint violation,
saturation and wall time. A single training trial is explicitly labeled
insufficient for generalization. These metrics do not establish native
runtime speed: Python objective evaluations, preprocessing, warm starts,
failed starts and native solver budgets must be counted under F03/F09 before
comparative claims. The seed tags the deterministic protocol; the current
L-BFGS-B stages do not use random starts.

## Native Floating-Root Fixture

The F04 native adapter evaluates the existing F02 controller and bounded
tuner on a contact-free MuJoCo 3.8 model with a free root, two hinges, and two
direct torque motors ($n_q=9$, $n_v=8$, $n_u=2$). A saved, independently
replayed torque history supplies the moving reference, frozen feedforward,
native-step clock, and time-varying feedback gains. Two training initial
states and one disjoint held-out initial state perturb the same model. The
only tuned parameters are bounded hip and knee feedback-row scales in
$[0,2]$; the controller observes the exact simulated complete state. Every
rollout records its post-limit torques and independently replays the complete
native integration state under the same model, time grid, and policy. Hip and
knee errors are evaluated using the native configuration tangent, including
the free-root quaternion, then separated into early and late phases.

In the source-bound synthetic fixture, the training objective decreases from
0.011786 to 0.007921, and held-out joint-error RMSE decreases from 0.11917
to 0.09647 rad when the frozen row scales change from (0.3, 0.3) to
(1.3, 1.3). Two block checkpoints are accepted; joint refinement exhausts
its budget, so this is an accepted bounded candidate rather than converged
joint optimization. The tuner performs 192 training and four held-out native
evaluations, including a post-fit baseline diagnostic. It observes 174
distinct applied-input histories and zero complete-state replay difference
at the tested precision. Its roughly 5.96 s wall-clock measurement includes
trial preflight, successful and failed tuner evaluations, diagnostics,
held-out replay, and export, but excludes teacher generation and process
startup. These numbers describe one small synthetic run, not a golf-swing
matching latency or algorithm comparison.

At a separately frozen teacher trajectory, symmetric single-motor input
interventions produce the hip/knee joint response (rad/N m)

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
0.16586 & -0.05492 \\
-0.06110 & 0.31150
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Both off-diagonal terms demonstrate dynamic cross-response in this specified
plant. This intervention is distinct from residual covariance and from the
loss Jacobian with respect to feedback gains. A local two-parameter response
Jacobian has nonzero singular values, but population-level identifiability and
uncertainty remain unavailable without capture noise, resampling, independent
swings, and alternate model parameters. No human neural causation is inferred.
The receipt is `docs/development/feedback_controls/F04_NATIVE_COUPLING_RECEIPT_MJ38.json`;
the exact reproduction command is in the associated turnover note.

## Coupling, Perturbation and Identifiability

At the accepted **frozen** controller, centered or bound-aware one-sided finite
differences estimate the scaled phase/group response
$A_{pgi}=D_{ii}\partial L_{pg}/\partial x_i$. Off-diagonal blocks of $A$
measure how a parameter group changes another group's loss. The reported
cross-Hessian blocks are finite differences of the *scalar training objective*
$D\nabla_x^2J D$, not a Gram surrogate. SVD of the response Jacobian flags
locally rank-deficient gain directions. A bounded diagnostic evaluation budget
prevents an accidental quadratic explosion in expensive plant rollouts.

Pooled covariance and within-phase covariance are reported separately because
phase shifts can create apparent cross-system correlation without within-phase
coupling. Neither covariance nor a local loss derivative identifies a causal
human neural loop. Gain, feedforward and unmeasured disturbances can compensate
one another; feedforward stays frozen and is not jointly identified here.
Perturbation evidence first evaluates the **same frozen controller** on altered
trials, then labels a separate refit and its scaled parameter shift. Matching
after refit is compensation evidence, not robustness of the frozen controller.
Parameter order, group, kind and scale must match before comparing a perturbation.

## Reproduction and Release Boundary

Run `python -m pytest tests/unit/motion_matching/test_control_loop_tuning.py -q --no-cov`
for the analytic coupled/uncoupled Hessian, phase-confounded
covariance, cross-block rejection, constraint and solver-failure retention,
heldout reduced/full, and actual F02 two-coordinate plant checks. Coordinates
are radians, speeds radians/second, time seconds and direct actuator efforts
N m in the synthetic fixture. The native model topology, frames, units,
capture timing, contact/force observations, full-horizon replay, and independent
muscle evidence remain prerequisites. No calibration, six-engine parity,
biomechanical validity or design-manual publication approval follows from this
software demonstration; the calculation registry remains blocked.
